caption: A toy fishing rod with a magnet on its line is dangled over paper fish fitted with steel clips, and a fish jumps up to the magnet and hangs from it.

sa.check: A toy fishing rod with a magnet on its line.
Paper fish fitted with steel clips lie below.
The magnet is dangled over the fish.
A fish jumps up to the magnet and hangs from it.
The fish attaches by its clip.
The dangle comes first and the jump follows.

pc.expect: The fish lie still until the magnet is close, then one leaps by its clip to the magnet; fish away from the magnet stay put.
pc.fail: A fish jumps while the magnet is still high above; or fish across the pool slide toward the rod; or fish move before the magnet is lowered; or a fish jumps by its tail with the clip untouched.

pc.expect: Once the clip meets the magnet the fish hangs from it and rises with the line as the rod is lifted, staying attached until pulled off.
pc.fail: The clip touches the magnet and the fish drops back; or the fish hangs a gap below the magnet without touching it; or the fish rises beside the magnet unattached; or the fish stays in the air when the rod is moved away.

pc.expect: The line hangs straight down from the rod tip with the magnet at its end; the fish hangs below the magnet; anything that comes loose falls.
pc.fail: The line stands out sideways or curves upward; or the fish hangs above the magnet; or a fish that comes off floats; or the magnet rises up the line.

pc.expect: The fish are paper cut-outs that flex and swing; the line is a limp thread; the rod is a rigid stick.
pc.fail: A fish is a rigid slab; or the line stands stiff like wire; or the rod bends double under a paper fish; or the fish stretches.

pc.expect: The fish on the magnet is one of the fish from below; fish keep their number; nothing merges or passes through the floor.
pc.fail: A fish appears on the magnet from nowhere; or a fish vanishes; or two fish merge; or the magnet passes through the floor of the pool.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The fish's colours, the rod and the pool stay the same.
pc.fail: A fish changes colour or shape; or the rod changes colour; or the pool changes.

note: Who holds the rod is not judged.
